title: Lightweight Lanes PRD — Acceptance Criteria and 'First 10K' Launch Checklist
creator: Asha Patel
overview: This PRD defines a minimal, cost-optimized hosted endpoint bundle (the 'Lightweight Lanes') targeting low-latency short-context workloads. The goal is to offer a constrained, predictable API surface for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank that is cheaper and faster than full-featured endpoints while retaining Redwood's operational guarantees. The initial launch ("First 10K") will focus on onboarding early adopters and validating performance/telemetry before broader availability.
goals: Deliver a compact hosted endpoint bundle optimized for short sequences (<=256 tokens) with fast cold-starts and predictable per-token cost
Provide conservative behavioral contracts for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank that simplify product integration and evaluation
Capture telemetry and cost signals to validate 30-50% unit-cost reduction for target workloads compared to standard hosted endpoints
Enable a controlled progressive rollout with eval gates and the ability to rollback to standard endpoints seamlessly
non_goals: Not intended to replace full-featured hosted endpoints for long-context or multimodal workloads
Does not include advanced structured-output or tool-calling in initial launch
No enterprise-dedicated capacity or VPC/private package at launch — this is hosted-only
user_stories: As a product engineer, I want a low-cost generation endpoint for short chat replies so I can power ephemeral conversational UI features within budget
As an ML engineer, I want embeddings optimized for short texts with predictable cosine similarity behavior so retrieval pipelines are stable
As a platform engineer, I want clear telemetry and guardrails so I can measure latency/cost regressions and control rollout
requirements: API compatibility: same REST/SDK surface as hosted generation/embedding endpoints with a new 'lane' query param (lane=lightweight)
SLO targets: 95th percentile tail latency < 120ms for short-generation calls (<=256 tokens) in regional zones under nominal load
Cost profile: unit cost target between 40-60% of standard hosted gen endpoint for typical short-chat workload (based on token size distribution histogram)
Behavioral contract: deterministic response shape for same prompt and model-version pinning; no support for function/tool calling in initial lane
Model variants: launch with two verified model variants (quantized and fp16) chosen by runtime routing for latency/cost tradeoffs
Quotas: default per-account rate limits aligned with free-tier and paid tiers; first 10K requests reserved for the pilot cohort
Telemetry: per-request fields for lane, model_variant, kernel_profile, batching_bucket, latency_ms, token_count, and cost_estimate
Docs: Quickstart and migration guide, cost calculator, and eval probe examples for each interaction type
acceptance_criteria: API contract: calling the standard /v1/generate with lane=lightweight returns valid tokens and header X-Redwood-Lane=lightweight
Latency: in regional staging, p95 latency for a canonical short-chat probe <= 120ms over a 24h continuous run
Cost: synthetic workload (samples matching production short-chat distribution) shows >= 30% lower average token cost vs baseline gen endpoint

Quality: eval suite (1000 prompts per interaction type) shows no more than 3% degradation in top-level semantic similarity for embeddings and no more than 5% drop in human-pref scoring for short-chat generation vs baseline model
Stability: no user-facing errors (5xx) above 0.05% of requests during a 48-hour soak in staging under 2x expected traffic
Observability: dashboards and alerts created for lane-specific SLOs and cost anomalies, and smoke-runbook documented
Docs & SDK: migration guide and code snippets added to SDKs and Console usage panel; docs reviewed and approved by DX lead
Security: security review completed and any required KMS/PII guidance added to docs
launch_checklist: Create lane registry entry and schema for lane=lightweight in API gateway
Runtime: validate kernel selection logic for short-sequence fast-paths and enable quantized variant
Routing: implement policy to route pilot accounts to lightweight lane; fallback to standard endpoints on capacity pressure
Telemetry: add lane-specific tags to ingestion pipeline and validate dashboard ingestion for 24h smoke-run
Docs: publish quickstart + migration guide + cost comparison table
SDKs: add convenience param and test examples in JS and Python SDKs; open PRs and get DX approval
Evals: run the 3 eval suites (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) and upload results to eval dashboard
QA: run cross-region canary for 72h at 0.5x expected load and record incidents
Legal/Security: complete security review, update DPA note for pilot where applicable
Billing: add unit-cost calculation in billing pipeline and create cost-visibility in Console
Rollout: schedule pilot cohort activation for 'First 10K' with customer communications draft
Playbooks: publish rollback and degradation playbooks; set on-call rotation for first-week monitoring
Telemetry Alerts: set thresholds for p95 latency, error-rate, and cost-per-token deviation > 15%
Support: train CS and Solutions on lane limitations and migration guidance
rollout_plan: Phase A: Internal pilot with Redwood apps + selected customers (First 10K requests) for 2 weeks. Phase B: Widen to beta customers with usage caps and continuous eval gating (2–4 weeks). Phase C: General availability with tiered pricing if all acceptance gates pass. Each phase requires a successful eval run and no critical incidents in the previous phase.
telemetry_and_traces: Event schema: add 'lane' and 'model_variant' to request event; emit kernel_profile and batching_bucket
Dashboards: p95/p99 latency, error-rate, cost-per-1000-tokens, model-variant split
Alerting: automated alert when cost-per-token deviates >15% vs baseline for 4 consecutive 5m buckets
dependencies: ENG-84219: telemetry ingestion pipeline lane tagging
ENG-84901: SDK convenience param and backwards-compatible change
PM-231000: pilot customer recruitment and comms
risks_and_mitigation: Behavioral degradation risk: mitigate by conservative model-variant selection and running evals with production-like prompts
Cost underestimation: maintain billing shadowing for 2 weeks before billing users; enable cost caps per account
Operational instability at scale: start with pilot 'First 10K' and extend only after 72h canary and load tests
Confusion with existing endpoints: explicit SDK and Console notices; X-Redwood-Lane response header included
decision_log: 2025-02-12: Decided to restrict initial lane to short-context (<256 tokens) to simplify kernel and batching choices — recorded by PM and runtime leads
2025-02-18: Chose to exclude function/tool-calling in initial pass to reduce surface area for evaluation
2025-02-25: Two model variants selected after perf sweep: rwd-mini-quant and rwd-mini-fp16
open_questions: Should we enable a per-account opt-in toggle in Console or rely on API param only? (tbh: prefer both for visibility)
What is the plan for rate-limiting policies if customers exceed lightweight lane quotas? Immediate fallback or throttled queuing?
Do we expose a recommended tokenization guide for customers migrating from standard endpoints?
